title: Claude Certified Architect - Foundations
goal: Pass the Claude Certified Architect - Foundations exam

exam.name: Claude Certified Architect - Foundations (CCA-F)
exam.verify_note: Domains, weights, format and the 720/1000 scaled pass mark come from third-party summaries of Anthropic's exam guide (v1.0, July 2026). A scaled score is not a plain percentage, so 0.72 is approximate. Confirm everything against Anthropic's official exam guide, then edit and re-import.

concepts.title: Workflows versus agents
concepts.objective: Decide when a fixed workflow, a single model call or an autonomous agent fits a problem, weighing cost, latency and control.

concepts.title: Prompt chaining, routing and parallelization
concepts.objective: Apply prompt chaining, routing and parallelization (sectioning and voting), and say what each trades off.

concepts.title: The agent loop: tool calls, results and stop reasons
concepts.objective: Trace the loop in which the model requests a tool, the client runs it and returns the result, until the stop reason says the turn is done.

concepts.title: Orchestrator-workers and subagent delegation
concepts.objective: Design an orchestrator that splits a task, delegates to worker agents with focused context, and merges their results.

concepts.title: Evaluator-optimizer loops and self-checks
concepts.objective: Use a generator and an evaluator in a loop, with clear criteria and a stopping rule.

concepts.title: Coordinating multiple agents
concepts.objective: Coordinate several agents through shared state, handoffs and isolated contexts, and recognise failure modes such as duplicated work and lost context.

concepts.title: Human checkpoints and permissions for agents
concepts.objective: Place approvals, permission policies and checkpoints where an agent's actions are risky or irreversible.

concepts.title: Building agents with the Claude Agent SDK
concepts.objective: Build an agent on the Claude Agent SDK with its built-in tools, custom tools, permissions and sessions.

concepts.title: Choosing where an agent runs
concepts.objective: Choose between a Messages API loop, the Agent SDK, Claude Code and hosted agents for a given deployment.

concepts.title: CLAUDE.md memory files and their hierarchy
concepts.objective: Write effective CLAUDE.md files and know how user, project and local memory combine.

concepts.title: Settings scopes and permission rules
concepts.objective: Configure settings at user, project and local scope, and write allow, ask and deny permission rules.

concepts.title: Hooks: events, matchers and blocking
concepts.objective: Use hooks on events such as PreToolUse, PostToolUse and SessionStart to enforce rules, block actions or add context.

concepts.title: Skills and slash commands
concepts.objective: Package a repeatable workflow as a skill or slash command, with arguments, allowed tools and supporting files.

concepts.title: Subagents in Claude Code
concepts.objective: Define subagents with their own instructions, tools and model, and delegate work to them to protect the main context.

concepts.title: Connecting MCP servers to Claude Code
concepts.objective: Add MCP servers at the right scope, share them through .mcp.json, and control their tools with permissions.

concepts.title: Plugins and marketplaces
concepts.objective: Bundle skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers into a plugin and distribute it through a marketplace.

concepts.title: Headless mode and CI automation
concepts.objective: Run Claude Code non-interactively (print mode, output formats, permission settings) in scripts and CI pipelines.

concepts.title: Effective workflows: plan, context and verification
concepts.objective: Use plan mode, focused context, tests and verification steps to get reliable results on real codebases.

concepts.title: Clear, direct instructions with context
concepts.objective: Write prompts that state the task, audience, constraints and success criteria explicitly.

concepts.title: Few-shot examples
concepts.objective: Choose and format examples that steer output without the model copying them too closely.

concepts.title: Structuring prompts with XML tags
concepts.objective: Separate instructions, context and data with XML tags, and ask for output in tagged sections.

concepts.title: System prompts and roles
concepts.objective: Decide what belongs in the system prompt and what in the user turn, and use roles effectively.

concepts.title: Extended thinking and effort
concepts.objective: Use extended or adaptive thinking and effort settings for hard problems, and know their cost and latency effects.

concepts.title: Structured outputs and JSON schemas
concepts.objective: Get reliably structured output with JSON schemas or tool definitions, and validate it.

concepts.title: Prompting with long documents
concepts.objective: Place long documents before the question, have the model quote relevant passages first, and ground answers in the provided text.

concepts.title: Defining tools: names, descriptions and input schemas
concepts.objective: Define tools with clear names, detailed descriptions and precise JSON input schemas.

concepts.title: Designing tools the model uses well
concepts.objective: Design tools at the right granularity, with unambiguous parameters and error messages the model can act on.

concepts.title: Tool results, errors and parallel tool calls
concepts.objective: Return tool results and errors (is_error) correctly, and handle several tool calls in one turn.

concepts.title: Controlling tool use: tool_choice and strict schemas
concepts.objective: Steer whether and which tools are used and enforce schemas with strict mode, noting which models restrict forced tool choice.

concepts.title: Server tools: web search, web fetch and code execution
concepts.objective: Use Anthropic-hosted tools and explain how their results differ from client tools.

concepts.title: MCP architecture: hosts, clients and servers
concepts.objective: Explain how MCP hosts, clients and servers connect, and why MCP standardises tool integration.

concepts.title: MCP primitives: tools, resources and prompts
concepts.objective: Choose between exposing a capability as an MCP tool, a resource or a prompt.

concepts.title: MCP transports, authentication and security
concepts.objective: Choose stdio or streamable HTTP transport, secure remote servers with OAuth, and guard against prompt injection through tool results.

concepts.title: Context windows and token budgets
concepts.objective: Budget tokens across instructions, history, documents and output, and know what happens when the window fills.

concepts.title: Prompt caching
concepts.objective: Structure prompts for cache hits (stable prefix first, breakpoints) and estimate the savings.

concepts.title: Managing context in long tasks: compaction, editing and memory
concepts.objective: Keep long agent runs within the window using compaction, context editing, subagents and memory files.

concepts.title: Retrieval and grounding
concepts.objective: Retrieve and inject relevant knowledge, cite sources, and ground answers to reduce hallucination.

concepts.title: Success criteria and evaluations
concepts.objective: Define measurable success criteria and build code-graded, model-graded and human evals to compare prompts and models.

concepts.title: Errors, rate limits, retries and streaming
concepts.objective: Handle API errors, rate limits and overloads with retries and backoff, and stream long responses.

concepts.title: Guardrails against hallucination, jailbreaks and prompt injection
concepts.objective: Reduce hallucinations, resist jailbreaks and prompt injection, and keep agents within policy.

concepts.title: Choosing models and settings for cost and latency
concepts.objective: Trade off model, effort, caching and batch processing against quality, cost and latency.
